title: Sodium Bicarbonate for In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Randomized Clinical Trial
shortTitle: BIHCA: routine bicarbonate did not improve sustained ROSC
summary: In this double-blind trial at 21 Danish hospitals, routine IV sodium bicarbonate did not improve sustained ROSC after in-hospital cardiac arrest. Of 913 randomized patients, 779 were eligible for the primary analysis.
whyItMatters: The findings argue against routine empiric bicarbonate during in-hospital arrest. They do not resolve treatment for specific indications such as selected poisonings.
limitations: Not powered to establish differences in survival or neurologic recovery. In-hospital arrest and postrandomization exclusions limit broader application.
population: Adults with in-hospital arrest who had received at least one dose of epinephrine.
intervention: Up to 100 mmol IV sodium bicarbonate.
findings: Alkalosis and hypernatremia were more common with bicarbonate.
evidenceNotes: Abstract reviewed; full text unavailable. Publisher abstract and PubMed abstract reviewed. Publisher confirms June 11 first-online date. PMC manuscript was marked unavailable until December 11, 2026, so it was not treated as currently accessible.
